title: Booze Buddy
summary: A UX-focused mobile app prototype promoting safer drinking habits for university students navigating social drinking culture.
overview: The project was created to explore how design can address social drinking in student life. Through this project, I aimed to apply UX principles to promote harm reduction and social connection, focusing on user-centered design practices.
problem: How might we support young adults in developing healthier drinking habits while still feeling socially confident?
objective: To promote safe and mindful drinking by reducing risks through accessible tools that enable real-time decision-making.
solution: Booze Buddy meets students where they are — real-time drink tracking, a help center, and safer choices without sacrificing social confidence.

title: Neko Beat
summary: A rhythm game exploring Parkinson's through controlled friction — designed in Figma and built with p5.js using Cursor.
overview: Built for a design brief on representing a human condition through interaction. I led visual and interaction design, then co-developed the game in p5.js with Cursor — using AI to implement HUD, controls, and gameplay systems from design decisions.
problem: Parkinson's is widely recognized but rarely understood experientially — most representations focus on symptoms, not the lived difficulty of intentional movement and timing.
objective: Design a rhythm game that introduces controlled friction in timing and coordination, while staying engaging and playable.
solution: Notes travel down lanes toward a hit bar. Players start with F and J, then unlock more keys in later levels. Mistimed presses create friction that echoes disrupted motor control — not as a clinical simulation, but as a felt timing challenge.

challenges.title: AI-assisted development
challenges.body: Used Cursor to turn design ideas into working code — multi-file edits for score/combo HUD, pause overlay, mute controls, and keyboard instruction clarity. I directed the gameplay intent; AI accelerated implementation across HTML, CSS, and sketch.js.

challenges.title: Controls & coordination
challenges.body: Players start with F and J (left/right hand), then later levels add more keys. Split-hand timing forces bilateral coordination under pressure.

challenges.title: Visual language
challenges.body: Synthwave neon and kawaii characters keep the tone approachable, so the friction feels like a game challenge rather than a clinical demo.
